key_insight: PulmoSight-XAI combines multi-view CNN ensembles, attention-based feature fusion, and stacked gradient-boosting meta-learners to improve multi-label chest X-ray classification while keeping predictions explainable.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more accurate and transparent thoracic disease screening on chest radiographs, especially when multiple pathologies co-occur.
method: View-specific ensembles trained separately on frontal and lateral X-rays
Multi-scale feature fusion with CBAM attention to preserve and emphasize pathology-relevant features
Two-level meta-learning with TTA, uncertainty features, and gradient boosting plus alpha blending
evidence_signal: On a large-scale CheXpert-style dataset, the model reported macro-average AUROC scores of 0.9319 for frontal views and 0.9154 for lateral views, with seven attribution methods showing anatomically consistent explanations.
watch_item: Performance and explainability were demonstrated on retrospective data, so external validation and workflow testing are still needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: PulmoSight-XAI: An Explainable Multi-View Attention Ensemble with Gradient Boosting Meta-Learning for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification
